title: Open problem: Are non-warmup process executions on JIT-compiling virtual machines largely due to JIT com
statement: Are non-warmup process executions on JIT-compiling virtual machines largely due to JIT compilation events - that is, to the virtual machine's own profile-guided recompilation - or to something outside the compiler? STATED ON BARRETT ET AL.'S OWN TERMS: this is their Hypothesis H3 restricted to its JIT disjunct, which they separated and examined on its own ("we take two VMs and separate out the time taken to perform Garbage Collection (GC) and JIT compilation. These two factors explain only some of the effects we see") and then declared unsettled, with the scope qualifier they attach to it. WHAT IS ALREADY PARTLY ANSWERED, so that none of it is redone: Barrett et al. give a split correlational result (Figure 7's slowdown at iteration #199 "correlates with two immediately preceding JIT compilation events", under their own "we make no claim that they prove causation", against Section 5.2's "in many cases such as Figure 8 neither JIT compilation, nor garbage collection, are sufficient to explain odd behaviours"); Antoch et al. 2026 dissect one recurrent change with "No extra dynamic compilation event and no extra garbage collection cycle" and shift it by a heap-size intervention instead; and Zheng, Bulej & Binder, "An Empirical Study on Deoptimization in the Graal Compiler", ECOOP 2017, DOI 10.4230/LIPIcs.ECOOP.2017.30, report scalac averaging "10 deoptimizations per iteration ... even past the 15th iteration" while finding the deoptimization policy's effect on the steady-state mean negligible. COMPUTABLE PART, and it is the tractable leg: a day-sized observational re-analysis of Antoch et al.'s released measurement package - per-execution changepoint classification against per-execution compilation and deoptimization event counts, reporting the association and its confidence interval at the execution grain, which no opened source prints. PROPOSED BUT GATED ROUTE: the three-arm interventional design (live recompilation; a per-method plan pinned from iteration 1 with adaptive recompilation disabled; a sham freeze applied only after the pilot's last observed compilation) over a rule-generated subset of Barrett's VM x benchmark matrix at fixed iteration count. THE GATE IS REAL: no current release of any VM in that matrix has been shown to install a recorded per-method plan and then make no further compilation decision - HotSpot's stop-recompiling state is interpreter fallback or repeated deopt logic, the only confirmed instrument is Jikes RVM on a 2007 build, and for the two tracing JITs "per-method plan" has no referent. A frozen arm that fails to converge therefore does NOT locate the cause outside the compiler, because deoptimization continues under a freeze and leaves the method interpreted.

inputs.source_showing_it_is_open: Barrett, Bolz-Tereick, Killick, Mount & Tratt, "Virtual Machine Warmup Blows Hot and Cold", OOPSLA 2017, DOI 10.1145/3133876, read in the authors' own LaTeX source (warmup.tex, 108,576 bytes) independently by two readers (LATEGATE4-10-1, LATEGATE4-10-2): Section 5.2, "The large number of non-warmup cases in our data led us to make the following hypothesis: H3 Non-warmup process executions are largely due to JIT compilation or GC events", then "we feel unable to validate or invalidate Hypothesis H3. Whilst some non-warmups are plausibly explained by GC or JIT compilation events, many are not, at least on HotSpot and PyPy"; Section 9.1.1 names the mechanism, "VMs have many counters which, when they exceed a certain threshold, cause the VM to change behaviour (e.g. (re)compile code ...)". Still open in public discourse with the flag-flip intervention performed but uncontrolled: hotspot-dev, May 2016, "I then tried turning off Tiered Compilation ... and the problem went away", with a HotSpot developer replying "A comparison between +TieredCompilation and -TieredCompilation might be very informative". Antoch et al. 2026 (OOPSLA, DOI 10.1145/3798236 as printed on the document; 10.1145/3839448 in a listing) neither pose nor settle it: its "a definitive confirmation for a specific workload and platform can only be given by additional experiments" is an external-validity disclaimer.
inputs.tier: A for the observational re-analysis of Antoch et al.'s released package; B for the three-arm interventional contrast, which is crisp in form but gated on an instrument no current matrix VM is known to have
inputs.how: Work it as PROMPT.md describes. Open the source first and confirm the problem is still open. State exactly what you established and what you did not.
